Every green capture the bundle actually carries for the shipped bytes shows 356/0: green-panel9-sh.log and green-panel9-ps1.log both end RESULT: 356 passed, 0 failed and both already contain the round-10 TEST-059 live-family assertion, and mutation-proofs-round7.log, whose trailer records restored sha256 a3d765814dfff390ac93577cb22fb33efcde50da27dc628e23aa41c27a094d85 (the shipped resolver hash in the Outputs table and in investigation.md), reports 356 passed 0 failed for its two behaviour-preserving mutants. investigation.md and the round-11 section of the implementation report both say 356. The contract also cites verification/T-007/mutation-proofs-test059.log as the non-vacuity proof for TEST-059; no such path exists among the declared outputs, the file is mutation-proofs-round7.log, and mutation-proofs-test059.log occurs exactly once in the whole bundle, in this comment. Compounding both, the declared green_evidence paths themselves (verification/qg/T-007/focused-tests-sh.log and -ps1.log) are not in the bundle, so the only description available of what they contain is this comment, and that description contradicts the shipped state. A gate consumer following the contract reaches a nonexistent proof file and a tally that does not match the code under review; on a high-risk Security-Sensitive task the record that two required checks passed at the shipped bytes cannot be confirmed from the artifact that declares it. This is the same amendment-propagation class the report names eleven times: round 11 carried 356 into the report and investigation.md and left the contract at 355.

Same stale tally in a declared output with a recorded SHA: the entry says sh/ps1 both 355 passed / 0 failed. It also says non-vacuity was proved by five mutations and enumerates bare-unlink rollback, skipped journal write, skipped post-publication recheck, digest-only step 13, and the TEST-059 injection, omitting the round-8 mutant that returns resolver-evidence.yaml to the rollback set, which is the one mutant tied to the Critical this task most recently closed and which the post-publication case does kill.

States six new fixture directories (listed under Outputs). The Outputs table enumerates ten fixture directories, and the CHANGELOG entry independently says fixture total is ten. The Tests Added Or Updated section likewise lists only six. The four containment-regression fixtures added in panel rounds 1 to 5 (journal-target-escape, staging-parent-symlink, target-parent-symlink, journal-roundtrip-unresolved-repo) never reached this line.

findings.note: Test Result reads PASS (306 passed / 0 failed, both runtimes), the GREEN capture subsection reads 306 passed 0 failed, and the Regression Tests Run table reads block 306 and discovery 12. These are the pre-panel numbers, superseded only by prose many hundreds of lines later. The Snapshot Notice partly covers this, but the headline result of a report whose later sections say 356 is a reader trap rather than a snapshot.

The comment block introducing TEST-059 states: Scanned PATHS: the staged human-copy candidates, not the live plugins/sdd-quality-loop/scripts/ paths AC-059 prose names. The code below it no longer behaves that way: run_test_059 builds present_live from the three live twins and appends them to the scanned set, and its own inline comment (round 10) says so explicitly. The two comments contradict each other about the same function, forty lines apart.

The ruling-(b) rationale, recorded identically in the docstring, investigation.md and the report, justifies stopping resolution at the parent purely on write semantics: os.replace replaces the entry at the leaf and mkstemp targets the parent. Correct for writes. But _live_bytes does follow a leaf symlink when it captures the PRE image, so a symlink planted at a leaf publication target causes out-of-tree bytes to be copied into the repository-local pre/ backup and, on rollback, materialised as a regular file at the leaf name inside the tree. The docstring asserts reading cannot escape either, which is true of the destination but not of the source. Low impact given the attacker already needs repository write access and the single-writer disposition of round 2, but the read direction is asserted rather than analysed in the record the owner ruled on.

The two disclosed-uncovered changes are described accurately: mutant C restores the pre-round-9 journal-delete ordering and mutant D removes the nonce/batch-directory binding, and both runs stay at 356 passed 0 failed, which the log itself labels UNCOVERED with the reason and the fixture that would be needed. The disclosure is honest and is the right way to record this. It remains the case that a crash-window ordering fix and a security hardening on a Security-Sensitive write path ship with no fixture, on a task whose own risk rationale is irreversible filesystem damage.
